title: MAGE query and query result
description: A question asked of a model system, and the shape of the answer. Every query carries an explicit quantifier: it determines what counts as evidence, and conflating existential with universal is the error the workbench exists to make visible. Semantics in SEMANTICS.md section 7.

name.description: Human-facing question. Saved queries re-run on model change.

expect.description: Expected outcome, for a saved query used as a CI gate. Present means the query is an ASSERTION: a run whose outcome differs is a build failure. Absent means the query is exploratory and any outcome is reported without judgement. Values are holds/refuted/... and never true/false -- a bare boolean here is a YAML-coercion bug (V25).

quantifier.description: exists: a witness proves TRUE, exhaustive absence proves FALSE. forall: exhaustive satisfaction proves TRUE, a counterexample proves FALSE. Never inferred silently -- an ambiguous natural-language question triggers Clarification or a displayed interpretation (V21).

behaviorQuery.description: A question about executions. Safety and reachability only: fairness is unsupported, so 'can it reach X' is in scope and 'will it eventually reach X' is not.

form.description: reach: a configuration satisfying target is reachable. invariant: predicate holds in every reachable configuration. recurrence: the target is RE-ENTERED -- a target configuration, at least one step, another target configuration; evidence is a LASSO whose cycle is the target-to-target segment. repeatable-cycle: a genuinely repeated CONFIGURATION, which is what makes a cycle actually repeatable; a loop whose bounded variable strictly advances answers refuted here while recurrence answers holds. Two forms, because can-it-come-back and can-it-loop-indefinitely are different questions and a query must denote a question rather than a search strategy. deadend: a configuration with no enabled step exists. transition-live: a named transition is executable in some reachable configuration.

target.description: State predicate. Required for reach and recurrence.

predicate.description: State predicate asserted to hold. Required for invariant.

avoid.description: Configurations the trace must never pass through. A past-time question is NOT expressed here -- it compiles to an invariant over a history variable, and the compilation is disclosed (V23).

limit.description: Max configurations to explore. Exceeding it yields coverage.kind=bounded, and therefore result=inconclusive (V22) -- never 'no'.

predicate.description: Conjunction of atoms unless all-of/any-of/not is used. An atom's key names a machine state (document.state), an instance state (worker[1].state), a variable, or a derived value.

relation.description: Relation type traversed. A multi-hop form over a type with composition.path=forbidden is REFUSED, not answered (V7) -- outcome=unlicensed.

where.description: Join predicate over endpoint properties, e.g. source.classification > target.accepts. Well-typed only if both sides declare the SAME ordered domain (V20).

outcome.description: holds: the claim is established (a witness for exists, exhaustive satisfaction for forall). refuted: the claim is refuted (exhaustive absence for exists, a counterexample for forall). inconclusive: mandatory when coverage is bounded (V22). unlicensed: the model does not authorize the question -- a SUCCESSFUL result, not an error (V7, V24). Deliberately NOT true/false: there is no boolean result, only a claim plus coverage plus evidence -- and a bare `true`/`false` in YAML is implicit-typed to a boolean anyway (V25).

interpreted-as.description: The question actually evaluated, in plain language. Mandatory when the query came from natural language (V21).

formal-query.description: The query object actually executed. The UI exposes this beside the answer.

refusal.description: Why the model does not license the question. Required when outcome=unlicensed.

compilation.description: Disclosed rewrites, e.g. an auxiliary history variable added to answer a past-time question (V23).

evidence.description: A witness supports an existential; a counterexample refutes a universal. A lasso is required for recurrence.

cycle.description: The repeating suffix. Required when shape=lasso.

machines.description: Instances that moved. More than one means a declared synchronized event fired.
